clue.text: German pair meets good Austrian writer

parts.note: zwei is the German word for two, a pair

explanation.surface: A German couple is introduced to a decent Austrian author.
explanation.walkthrough: Stefan Zweig was an Austrian novelist and biographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stefan Zweig was a celebrated Austrian novelist and biographer of the interwar years.

clue.text: A tapa, doze disturbed a tap dance

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it are disturbed, knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone dozing after a Spanish snack is disturbed by tap dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges the letters of A TAPA DOZE.
explanation.definitionFit: The zapateado is a Spanish flamenco-style dance marked by rhythmic stamping of the heels, a kind of tap.

clue.text: English Navy way of surrealist

parts.note: RN stands for Royal Navy
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A British naval route somehow belongs to a surrealist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Max Ernst was a German surrealist artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a leading painter of the Surrealist movement.

clue.text: Presumably the answer to Keats's "Who are these coming to the sacrifice ?"

definitions.text: Presumably the answer to Keats's "Who are these coming to the sacrifice ?"

parts.words: Presumably the answer to Keats's "Who are these coming to the sacrifice ?"
parts.note: the line comes from Keats's ode on an urn from ancient Greece, so the procession pictured on it would be people of that land

explanation.walkthrough: The question is from Ode on a Grecian Urn, whose scene shows a sacrificial procession.
explanation.definitionFit: The figures painted on an urn from Greece would naturally be Greek people.

clue.text: Soothsayer suggests Eliot's Eppie and academician

parts.note: in George Eliot's Silas Marner, Eppie is the daughter of Godfrey Cass
RA, Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller is implied by a character from Silas Marner and a learned artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Eppie's birth surname is Cass, though she is raised by Silas Marner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra was the Trojan prophetess fated to foretell the truth and never be believed.

clue.text: Durrell protagonist in debacle at Cairo

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters debacle at

explanation.surface: A Lawrence Durrell character gets caught up in a fiasco in the Egyptian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Clea is the title character of the fourth novel of Durrell's Alexandria Quartet.
explanation.definitionFit: Clea is the painter who gives her name to the last book of Durrell's Alexandria Quartet.

clue.text: Decker's holiday? Cobblers

explanation.surface: A pun on a play's title and on a slang word for nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Dekker (spelt Decker here) wrote the comedy The Shoemaker's Holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Dekker's play is The Shoemaker's Holiday, and cobblers are people who mend footwear.

clue.text: "Ah, what — the sceptred race!/ Ah, what the form divine!" (W. S. Landor)

definitions.text: "Ah, what — the sceptred race!/ Ah, what the form divine!" (W. S. Landor)

parts.words: "Ah, what — the sceptred race!/ Ah, what the form divine!" (W. S. Landor)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the dash stands for the missing word in Landor's lament Rose Aylmer

explanation.walkthrough: Landor's poem Rose Aylmer begins 'Ah what avails the sceptred race'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means 'is of use', asking what good royal birth or beauty does.

clue.text: English provincial lady of spoiled valley and meadow

indicators.note: the word for valley is spoiled, its letters jumbled

parts.note: a dale is a valley
a field is a meadow

explanation.surface: A rural woman from England comes from a ruined valley and a pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' jumbles DALE into DELA. E. M. Delafield wrote Diary of a Provincial Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: E. M. Delafield, an English author, is best known for her Diary of a Provincial Lady.

clue.text: Jane's suggested boreal fury

parts.note: boreal means northern and fury means anger, together hinting at the title of a Jane Austen novel

explanation.walkthrough: Northern anger suggests Northanger, and Jane Austen's novel is Northanger Abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Austen's Gothic parody is titled after Northanger, a medieval monastery building turned country house.

clue.text: Wells inventor who exhibited teddidity

parts.note: points to the patent-medicine inventor nicknamed Teddy in H. G. Wells's Tono-Bungay

explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Edward, known as Teddy, sells the tonic Tono-Bungay in Wells's novel; the grid prints his surname with two letters swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Ponderevo, inventor of the quack remedy in Tono-Bungay, is nicknamed Teddy, hence teddidity.

clue.text: It came off the performer's cuff

definitions.text: It came off the performer's cuff

parts.words: It came off the performer's cuff
parts.note: something said off the cuff is improvised, so this is an unscripted remark by a performer

explanation.definitionFit: An improvised line, spoken off the cuff rather than from the script.

clue.text: Time note to sit up in passages where all take part

parts.note: UT is the old name for the note doh in sol-fa

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word sit is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician is told when to sit up during the full-orchestra passages.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the old sol-fa name for doh, a convention worth knowing; 'up' turns the word sit around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutti is a musical passage played by the whole ensemble together.

clue.text: 'Compared with Sheridan, all other managers were ——' (James Payn)

definitions.text: 'Compared with Sheridan, all other managers were ——' (James Payn)

parts.words: 'Compared with Sheridan, all other managers were ——' (James Payn)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the missing words mean people of little importance

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means insignificant people, as young fish are tiny beside grown ones.

clue.text: Decker's Cypriot hero could be nuts. Far out!

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow could be rearranged into the name

explanation.surface: A remark that a playwright's hero might be crazy: far out!
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges NUTS FAR OUT. Dekker's play Old Fortunatus is about a man of Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Dekker's comedy Old Fortunatus has as its hero a Cypriot granted a magic purse.

clue.text: Curious local token for Kingsley work

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd token from the area is used for a book by Kingsley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges LOCAL TOKEN. Alton Locke is Charles Kingsley's 1850 novel about a tailor-poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Kingsley's novel Alton Locke follows a Chartist tailor and poet.

clue.text: Kafka's rook

parts.note: a rook in chess is also called a castle, and Kafka wrote a novel of that title

explanation.definitionFit: Kafka's unfinished novel shares its name with the chess piece also called the rook.

clue.text: Snare, say, for writer who has succeeded with costly poison

definitions.text: writer who has succeeded with costly poison

indicators.note: say signals that the word for snare is spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: a web is a snare for flies

explanation.surface: A trap is mentioned for an author who did well with an expensive toxin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'costly poison' is Precious Bane, the novel by Mary Webb that made her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Webb's success was the novel Precious Bane, and precious bane means costly poison.

clue.text: French dramatist who knew how to conduct himself?

definitions.text: French dramatist who knew how to conduct himself?

parts.words: French dramatist who knew how to conduct himself?
parts.note: a French playwright whose surname is shared with a famous American orchestra conductor

explanation.walkthrough: Henri Bernstein was a French playwright; Leonard Bernstein conducted orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Bernstein wrote Parisian stage melodramas; the question mark nods to conductor Leonard of the same surname.

clue.text: South African poet, said to be a coming man

definitions.text: South African poet, said to be a coming man

parts.words: South African poet, said to be a coming man
parts.note: a South African poet whose clan, in the Scottish song, are said to be coming

explanation.walkthrough: Roy Campbell was a South African poet; the old Scots song is 'The Campbells are Coming'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Campbell was a South African poet, and the Scottish song announces his clan's arrival.

clue.text: War poet starts out with English name

indicators.note: the starts of the two words out and with are their first letters

explanation.surface: A poet of the trenches sets out with an English name.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilfred Owen was the leading English poet of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred Owen wrote poems of the First World War trenches such as Dulce et Decorum Est.

clue.text: Seth who offered better than cold comfort

definitions.text: Seth who offered better than cold comfort

parts.words: Seth who offered better than cold comfort
parts.note: points to the handsome Seth of Stella Gibbons's novel set on a farm of that comfortless name

explanation.walkthrough: Seth Starkadder is the brooding farm son in Stella Gibbons's Cold Comfort Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth is the smouldering younger son of the family in Stella Gibbons's comic novel Cold Comfort Farm.

clue.text: Singers meeting

parts.note: a gathering of sitters who join hands to contact the dead

explanation.walkthrough: A séance is a meeting of people seeking contact with spirits; the clue as held reads 'Singers', where 'Sitters', the usual word for séance participants, seems likely.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist session is a gathering whose participants are called sitters.

clue.text: "Boys and girls tumbling in the street, and playing were moving jewels" ()

definitions.text: "Boys and girls tumbling in the street, and playing were moving jewels" ()

parts.words: "Boys and girls tumbling in the street, and playing were moving jewels" ()
parts.note: a quotation whose author belongs in the empty brackets: it is from the Third Century of the seventeenth-century mystic's Centuries of Meditations

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Traherne wrote this line about his childhood vision in Centuries of Meditations.

clue.text: He alone concludes Gothic trilogy

parts.note: the third Gormenghast novel is named after its hero with the word alone

explanation.walkthrough: Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast books end with Titus Alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Groan is the hero of Peake's Gormenghast books, whose third volume is Titus Alone.

clue.text: Suit in which Sarah Battle perceived a hoary majesty

definitions.text: Suit in which Sarah Battle perceived a hoary majesty

parts.words: Suit in which Sarah Battle perceived a hoary majesty
parts.note: Charles Lamb's essay on Mrs Battle's opinions on whist praises the dignity of one card suit

explanation.walkthrough: In Lamb's essay Mrs Battle's Opinions on Whist she admires 'the hoary majesty of spades'.
explanation.definitionFit: The black suit of playing cards that Lamb's whist player admired for its dignity.

clue.text: Composer suggests dissolution of synod

indicators.note: dissolution breaks up the word synod so its letters reform

explanation.surface: A composer is hinted at by the breaking up of a church council.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir George Dyson was an English composer and director of the Royal College of Music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir George Dyson was an English composer of choral works such as The Canterbury Pilgrims.

clue.text: Article on unknown author

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An essay about a writer nobody can name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anonymous is used for a writer whose name is not known, shortened in citations.

clue.text: Mythical giant satellite

explanation.definitionFit: Titans were the giant elder gods of Greek myth, and Titan is Saturn's largest moon.

clue.text: Dramatist's state seen tense, overwrought

indicators.note: overwrought means agitated, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A playwright's condition is seen as tense and overwrought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwrought' rearranges SEEN TENSE. The playwright is Tennessee Williams, whose first name is an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is a US state and also the first name of playwright Tennessee Williams.

clue.text: Good man -odds on to make novelist

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
evens is betting odds of one to one

explanation.surface: A good man's chances are put on a bet to produce a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, the Scottish author of Kidnapped and Treasure Island.

clue.text: The French American novelist, diarist, revolutionary

parts.note: le is a French word for the
Anais Nin was an American novelist famous for her diaries

explanation.surface: A list of a French figure, an American writer, a diarist and a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Anaïs Nin wrote novels and celebrated published diaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik revolution of 1917 in Russia.
